newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices stabilise in week.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices stabilise in week.

text.p: Australian wool prices stabilised at sales in Sydney, Melbourne and Fremantle this week, the first of the 1997/98 season, Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said on Friday,
"After last week's price correction the market stabilised and closed on a firm note before the three week sale recess," Wesfarmers said in its weekly market report.
The Australian Council of Wool Exporters said the new season commenced on a positive note with auction prices steadying and firming after the roller coaster ride of the preceding weeks.
The eastern market indicator rose 10 cents to end the week at 716 cents a kg clean, up sharply from 598 cents a year ago.
The western market indicator fell 27 cents to 665 cents from the level of the last Fremantle sale two weeks ago.
A total of 127,015 bales were offered with a pass in rate of nine percent.
"Exporters felt that the market performed solidly, given the events of recent weeks and the large quantity of wool on offer," the council said
"There were reports of increased enquiry from overseas customers at the lower price basis, and competition in the market was widespread," it said.
